segments: The 37th {OCR?} of the Arab kings.
And in the Later Kanon there was severe cold,
and the river Tigris froze,
and heavy snow fell in Baghdad itself.
And in the year 458
458 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1377
1377 of the Greeks
(1066 of our Lord?), Sultan Alp Arslan went to Khwarazm,
and appointed his son Salar-Shah over it,
and he himself returned to Nishapur. And in this same year, about three hundred Armenian brigands gathered around the sons of Khazrig (Kharig) the Armenian,
and they used to lie in ambush in the mountains of Melitene,
and raided the region of Gubos and of Qlaudiya,
especially the monasteries.
For they entered the Monastery of Sargisiya,
and threw the bones of the martyrs upon the ground,
and took the reliquary.
And from Sangis (Singas), a village near the Monastery of Madiq (Madiq), they took crops worth a thousand and one hundred dinars, besides oxen and wine;
and from the monastery [they took goods] worth five hundred dinars.
Then the leaders of Melitene resolved to give them an allowance from Gubos and Qlaudiya.
And they also sent to the king and brought them a sigillion,
so that they should have four villages,
and not raid anymore.
However, they did not cease from their wickedness,
and set their sights upon the monastery of Mor Bar Sawma,
in order to seize it by stealth and fortify themselves in it.
And at that time, suddenly a report reached that the Turks
were again entering the region of Melitene.
And the people of Qlaudiya fled to the monastery,
and with them were ten of the Armenian thieves, while the rest lay in ambush on the mountain,
so that at night their companions would open [the gates] for them,
and they would rush in, enter, and take control.
And when John the monk, the steward, noticed this,
he took with him certain valiant men from Tel-Tawra, the blessed village,
who were present in the monastery,
and overpowered those ten.
And they threw them that very night from the cliff of the monastery,
without informing the abbot.
And when it was morning,
they were seen lying dead at the foot of the rock.
And their companions heard [of it] and fled.
And after some days,
as monks and servants were coming from Melitene to the monastery,
those brigands fell upon them,
and killed three monks and two servants.
